newsitem.title: INDIA: India alliance seen putting off oil price decision.
newsitem.headline: India alliance seen putting off oil price decision.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition is unlikely to decide at a scheduled meeting this week whether to raise oil prices to plug a mounting subsidy bill, a government official said.
"I doubt that they will decide on Friday," said the official, who asked not to be identified, on Tuesday.

The government owes state oil companies an estimated 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) in subsidies and the companies have complained that they cannot keep importing crude unless domestic prices are raised.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 15-party coalition has twice put off the decision on prices but had planned to tackle the subject at a meeting set for Friday in the capital.
Petroleum Minister Janeshwar Mishra said on Monday the ruling centre-left coalition might have to postpone this week's meeting because he could not attend.

The government official said the United Front's decision-making Steering Committee was still expected to meet on Friday, but would probably not take up the oil price issue as Mishra would be out of town attending a party meeting.
He said the ruling alliance intended to take a final decision on oil prices before parliament reconvenes for a month-long monsoon season on July 23.
The two-month-old government is deeply split over the issue, with communists vigorously opposed to any price increase, and Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in favour of moderate rises.
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) wants customs and excise duties on oil eliminated and has submitted an alternative plan to avoid higher petroleum prices, which it says would hurt the poor.
Any increase in petroleum product prices would be the second by the United Front in its one year in power.
Last July the government raised the price of gasoline by 25 percent and the prices of high-speed diesel, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for cooking, paraffin wax and fuel oil by 30 percent.
It was forced to scale back the rise in diesel prices to 15 percent after nationwide protests supported by left-wing parties. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
